title: Heavy hitters: sketch vs exact vs store and query (real collector containers)

panels.title: Three approaches to the same question: which routes are heavy hitters, and which are new?

sources A and B

Count-Min 4×512 + top-20 heap per 1-min window

route → count map per 1-min window

raw-generator-a/b
same points
→

→
prometheus-raw
stores every raw point, one sample each
→
query-job
PromQL top-20 once per window; new heavy hitters

Every stage is one pinned container. Traffic grows over 30 minutes: the rate per source doubles every 5 minutes (5k to 80k points/s), /new/hot-route takes 15% of traffic at minute 10, and the number of routes grows from 100,000 to 1,000,000 at minute 15. Each approach writes to its own Prometheus. raw-sink adds a point_slot label so points of one series at the same millisecond stay separate samples. hh-accuracy compares the sketch with exact; query-job compares store and query with exact and times every approach's query.

panels.title: Accuracy against exact
Heavy hitters (routes with >= 1% of the window's points): precision, recall, F1
panels.description: Truth: exact counts >= 1% of the window's points. Store and query loses accuracy only when points never reached prometheus-raw.

panels.title: Average relative count error of the heavy hitters found (ARE)
Traffic over time: volume and shape
End-to-end throughput: points per second each window delivered to the end of its pipeline
panels.description: Both sources together. The generators skip batches a pipeline cannot take, so a pipeline that falls behind delivers less. Store and query: points prometheus-raw acknowledged within 50 s of the window's end. A pipeline that stops reporting shows a gap after 2 minutes.

panels.title: Data shape: distinct routes per window (exact)
Query latency and data freshness (reported separately)
Query latency: time to run the query that returns a window's answer
panels.description: Measured by query-job once per window against each approach's own Prometheus. sketch and exact read the stored answer; store and query computes it from every raw sample (one PromQL top-k query). Includes refused and timed-out queries.

panels.title: Data freshness (ingestion lag): load time - event creation time, per point
panels.description: How long a point takes from its creation to being in its approach's Prometheus, p50 and p99 over the window's points. store and query: Prometheus's acknowledgement of the point minus its event time, measured for every point by raw-sink. sketch and exact: a point is in Prometheus once its window's answer is, so its lag is the time to the window's end plus the window's answer delay (points arrive evenly over the window). The answer delay is when the detector sent the answer; Prometheus stores it milliseconds later. Query latency is not included.

panels.title: Sketch: answer delay breakdown per window
panels.description: Seconds per segment after the window's end, until the answer goes to Prometheus. branch + to merge: the window's end until the last source's sketch reached the merge. merge: waiting for the other source's sketch (5 s timeout).

panels.title: Exact: answer delay breakdown per window
panels.description: Seconds per segment after the window's end, until the answer goes to Prometheus. branch + to merge: the window's end until the last source's sketch reached the merge. merge: waiting for the other source's sketch (5 s timeout).

panels.title: Store and query: time to store the window's last point
panels.description: The window's end until prometheus-raw acknowledged its last point (or raw-sink's 50 s timeout).
